content: A prominent example is the June 5, 2026, development regarding a proposed 12.5 percent tariff by the United States on imports from several countries, including South Africa [55] . This proposed tariff structure possesses the potential to significantly influence international trade flows, which could indirectly impact commodity transport demand [55] . In summary, while scattered indicators point toward growing pressures on transport capacity and rising logistics costs across the African continent, concrete and highly current data specific to South African commodity transport demand remains insufficient in globally focused reviews. The prevailing global capacity constraints, inflationary pressures, and regional cost escalations suggest a highly competitive and expensive logistics environment.
